claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
High-resolution TEM/SEM images can provide quantitative descriptors of chemical-fluctuation length scales.
Image-derived features can capture grain-boundary chemistry and nanoscale fluctuation-domain size, distribution, and contrast.
The image-derived descriptors encode the effects of mesoscale heterogeneity on dislocation motion.
The image-derived descriptors encode the effects of mesoscale heterogeneity on crack propagation.
Incorporating these descriptors into a physics-informed loss function will correct purely composition-based mechanical-property predictions.
The proposed framework will predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness with an average error of no more than 10% relative to experiments.
The proposed framework will reduce model-development time by at least 50%.
Model-development time will decrease from approximately eight weeks to approximately four weeks.
The proposed framework will outperform prior CALPHAD plus first-principles approaches.
The existing CALPHAD, first-principles, and conventional machine-learning pipeline has approximately 20% prediction error.
The existing baseline pipeline requires approximately eight weeks per development cycle.
The model will cease to be reliable for alloys lacking well-resolved hierarchical heterostructure features or multilevel chemical fluctuations.
The model will cease to be reliable when image resolution is worse than 1 nm per pixel.
Integration of imaging data into physics-informed models has received limited prior benchmarking in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The prospective benchmark will use 30 independently processed HfNbTiVAl10 specimens and blind predictions made before tensile and fracture testing.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires at least a 50% time reduction and the predicted outcome says development time is halved, but the falsification rule rejects the hypothesis only when savings are below 30%. A result with 30–49% savings would fail the stated hypothesis while escaping falsification.
